    Marko¶

    "Come as you are. Trade as you will. Leave richer than you arrived." — Inscription over Marko's central market gate

    An international trade hub and semi-republic on Kutten, unique among the nations of Ge'or. Marko is not a kingdom, not a tribe, not a colony — it is a merchant city-state governed by elected High Catmen rulers, where every species trades freely and no one asks where you came from.

    Marko is the most prominent settlement on Kutten — the desert continent's gateway to the world.

    Founding¶

    After the fall of Elvengar and the Kutten Catastrophe that desertified the continent, Kutten was abandoned for a century. When the toxic rains ceased and the air cleared, two groups saw opportunity in the wasteland:

    • Erisdarians — settlers from the Erisian Empire and the southern trade republics, hoping to claim abandoned elven lands.
    • Demon Continent settlers — colonists from Asatru and other demon nations, seeking new territory across the sea.

    Neither group could dominate the other. Instead of fighting, they traded. The settlement that became Marko was organized in 322 AGD — a formal recognition of what had already become the de facto arrangement: a neutral ground where Erisdarian and demonic interests could meet and profit.

    The High Catmen of Estran saw the opportunity before anyone else. Their merchant families moved in, established trade networks, and — through commerce, diplomacy, and sheer competence — rose to become Marko's ruling class. They have held that position ever since.

    Government¶

    Marko is a semi-republic. High Catmen are elected as rulers by a council of merchant families and guild representatives. The system is not democratic in the universal sense — voting power correlates with economic stake — but it is more open than any monarchy on Ge'or.

    The elected High Catmen rulers serve fixed terms. Their primary responsibility is maintaining Marko's neutrality and ensuring that commerce flows uninterrupted. War is bad for business. Marko has never started one.

    Trade¶

    Marko is the commercial hub of Kutten. Its trade networks span the known world:

    • Demon Continent — direct trade with Asatru, Maomodor Kingdom, Koebi Tribe, and others.
    • Yak Island — strong ties with Estran (the High Catmen homeland), Yakut, and Cubra Tribe.
    • West Erisdar — Demon's Horn, Augamouth, Xikxia, and Astravayne all trade through Marko.
    • Venner — a major trade partner. Vennerian ships are a common sight in Marko's harbors.

    Marko charges no tariffs on goods passing through its markets. It profits instead from banking, warehousing, and the services that naturally accumulate around a neutral trade hub.

    Foreign Relations¶

    • Estran — the closest ally. The High Catmen of Estran are Marko's ruling class; the two nations are effectively sister-states.
    • Venner — strong trade partnership. Venner values Marko as a neutral port.
    • Yakut — across the sea. Cordial trade relations.
    • Oda — orc kingdom to the northeast. Neutral but stable.
    • Malbodor — the Sandsmen kingdom. Limited interaction — Malbodor is insular.
    • New Elvengar — the elven restoration kingdom. Minimal contact.

    Society¶

    Marko is the most cosmopolitan city on Kutten — perhaps in the region. Its streets host:

    • High Catmen — the ruling merchant class.
    • Humans — Erisdarian traders, settlers, and bankers.
    • Demons — merchants and diplomats from the Demon Continent.
    • Orcs — traders from Augamouth, soldiers-for-hire.
    • Lesser Catmen — everywhere, as always, universally welcome.
    • Snake People — careful not to take sides in the sister-queen feud.
    • Sandsmen — rare, but the occasional desert guide or mineral trader.

    No species is turned away. No feud is imported. Marko's neutrality is absolute — and enforced by the simple fact that anyone who breaks it loses access to the most valuable market on Kutten.

    Religion¶

    Marko is the stronghold of Calism — the catmen philosophy-faith. Calism preaches pacifism, docility, and gentleness, seeking only to greaten oneself; it is ecumenical without holding all religions true. Marko's High Catmen rulers embody the faith's practical edge: gentle in trade, but strict — even cruel — toward anything self-destructive. The humans and other species of Marko keep Calism's firmer discipline; the catmen themselves live it lightly, playful and aloof, though they still find self-destructive behavior strange.
